newsitem.title: FINLAND: NORVESTIA SAYS INTERESTED IN AMER .
newsitem.headline: NORVESTIA SAYS INTERESTED IN AMER .

text.p: Finnish investment company Norvestia said in a statement on Thursday it was interested in becoming sporting goods group Amer's main owner and to bid for part of Amer's K shares.
"Norvestia has in the past few weeks gradually announced its interest to take the main owner's responsibity in Amer together with some current K-shareholder," it said.
"Norvestia's interest requires that Amer Group would use its right to redeem part of the K-shares," Norvestia said.

"Norvestia's effort is in this context to work together with present management to make Amer a shareholder-friendly public company aiming towards holding and investment activities with a clear preponderance in (current sporting goods operations)," Norvestia said.
The four associations which hold Amer's controlling K shares agreed on June 2 to sell shares giving a majority of votes to British investor Jonathan Bryan Guinness, third Lord Moyne.
Norvestia managing director Timo Loyttyniemi told Reuters that he believed a takeover was still possible, but gave no details on a possible bid.
"We have the impression that under these terms, this deal would be possible," he said.

"The intention is that the sellers as well as the other 14,000 shareholders and members of the board and the supervisory board shall find this solution more appealing than the alternative (selling to Guinness)," Norvestia said.
It said the market value of its assets on May 31 were 575 million markka, 283 million of which were liquid assets, and it had no interest-bearing debt.
Buying into Amer would be a long-term investment in accordance with Norvestia's present policy, and would not change its character as an investment company, it said.
